newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's RAG to boost coal imports.
newsitem.headline: Germany's RAG to boost coal imports.

text.p: German coal producer RAG, formerly known as Ruhrkohle AG, plans to increase coal imports over the next several years as German output is curtailed, RAG chairman Gerhard Neipp said on Tuesday.
RAG's imports should climb to between 20 million to 25 million tonnes a year by the year 2005, from a mere 5 million tonnes currently, Neipp said.

RAG also plans to invest in mines outside Germany. "Internationalisation will strengthen our competitiveness," he said. German hard coal costs several times as much as imports, but government subsidies even out the difference in the market price.
While German energy demand is stagnating, world demand for electricity is expected to rise 75 percent in the next 25 years, he said.
The German government's decision to curtail subsidies for coal mining will drive total domestic production down to 30 million tonnes annually from the current 50 million tonnes, Neipp said.
Demand, however, is expected to hold steady, so the Essen-based RAG, which supplies two-thirds of German hard-coal, will sharply boost imports to maintain market share, he said.
RAG at the start of this year set in motion the restructuring that will help it cope with the changing market, he said.
Non-mining activities already account for over 50 percent of sales, prompting last year's name change, and will continue to rise, he said.
The company has held its workforce flat at 102,000 over the past two years as growth in non-mining business offset the decline in mining business.
-- Terence Gallagher, Hanover Trade Fair Newsroom
